import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.16

by L. A. Kurdachenko

A class of groups is called a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking subgroups,
factor-groups, and direct products (Yu. M. Gorchakov, *Groups with Finite Classes of Conjugate
Elements*, Moscow, Nauka, 1978 (Russian)). It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a
direct variety. P. Hall (*J. London Math. Soc.*, **34**, no. 3 (1959), 289–304) showed that the
class of finite groups and the class of abelian groups taken together do not generate the class
of $FC$-groups as a direct variety, and it was shown in (L. A. Kurdachenko, *Ukrain. Math. J.*,
**39**, no. 3 (1987), 255–259) that the direct variety of $FC$-groups is also not generated by
the class of groups with finite derived subgroups. Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated
by the class of groups with finite derived subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups
having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

Here an $FC$-group is a group in which every element has only finitely many conjugates, and a
quasicyclic group is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$. "Direct product"
means the restricted direct product (only finitely many non-identity coordinates) over an
arbitrary index set: unrestricted Cartesian products of infinitely many non-abelian finite
groups are not $FC$-groups, so with unrestricted products the class of $FC$-groups would not be
a direct variety.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
open scoped RestrictedProduct
namespace Kourovka.«10.16»
universe u

blocks.code:
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite
blocks.docstring: A group $G$ is an $FC$-group if every element of $G$ has only finitely many conjugates.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `conjugatesOf`, `ConjClasses.carrier`, `Subgroup.centralizer`/`Subgroup.FiniteIndex` (equivalent reformulation via centralizers of finite index, but less direct).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.16».IsFCGroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of FC-group (every element has finitely many conjugates). Defined as `∀ g, (conjugatesOf g).Finite` using Mathlib's `conjugatesOf`.

blocks.name: IsFCGroup

blocks.code:
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ))
blocks.docstring:
A group is *quasicyclic* if it is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$,
i.e. isomorphic to the group of all complex $p^n$-th roots of unity, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `rootsOfUnity` (used), `CommGroup.primaryComponent ℂˣ p` (needs a `Fact p.Prime` instance; equivalent), `AddCircle`/ℚ⧸ℤ p-torsion; no `IsLocallyCyclic` exists for an intrinsic characterisation.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.16».IsQuasicyclic
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no Prüfer p-group / quasicyclic group. Defined as: for some prime p, G is isomorphic to `⨆ n, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ`, the group of all complex p^n-th roots of unity (the standard model of ℤ(p^∞)).

blocks.name: IsQuasicyclic
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *quasicyclic* if it is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$,
i.e. isomorphic to the group of all complex $p^n$-th roots of unity, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. -/
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ))

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib; varieties of groups are not formalised.

blocks.name: GroupClass
blocks.text:
/-- A class of groups (in the universe `u`), given as a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type (u + 1) :=
  ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

blocks.code:
structure IsDirectVariety (𝓒 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop where
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  subgroup : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  quotient : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝓒 G → 𝓒 (G ⧸ N)
  restrictedProduct : ∀ {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, 𝓒 (G i)) → 𝓒 (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))])
blocks.docstring:
A class of groups is a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking isomorphic copies,
subgroups, factor-groups, and restricted direct products $\prod^{\text{res}}_{i \in I} G_i$
(all $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ with $x_i = 1$ for all but finitely many $i$) over arbitrary index
sets $I$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `RestrictedProduct` (used for the products); no notion of variety/direct variety of groups exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.16».IsDirectVariety
justification.why_needed: Gorchakov's 'direct variety': a class of groups closed under isomorphic copies, subgroups, factor-groups and restricted direct products (Mathlib's `RestrictedProduct` with `⊥` subgroups and the cofinite filter) over arbitrary index sets in the same universe.

blocks.name: IsDirectVariety
blocks.text:
/-- A class of groups is a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking isomorphic copies,
subgroups, factor-groups, and restricted direct products $\prod^{\text{res}}_{i \in I} G_i$
(all $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ with $x_i = 1$ for all but finitely many $i$) over arbitrary index
sets $I$. -/
structure IsDirectVariety (𝓒 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop where
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  subgroup : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  quotient : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝓒 G → 𝓒 (G ⧸ N)
  restrictedProduct : ∀ {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, 𝓒 (G i)) → 𝓒 (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))])

blocks.docstring:
The direct variety generated by a class of groups `𝓧`: the smallest direct variety
containing `𝓧`, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing `𝓧`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Subgroup.closure`-style closure operators; nothing for classes of groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.16».directVarietyClosure
justification.why_needed: The direct variety generated by a class 𝓧: intersection of all direct varieties containing 𝓧 (impredicative smallest-class definition).

blocks.name: directVarietyClosure
blocks.text:
/-- The direct variety generated by a class of groups `𝓧`: the smallest direct variety
containing `𝓧`, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing `𝓧`. -/
def directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) : GroupClass.{u} :=
  fun G _ => ∀ 𝓒 : GroupClass.{u},
    IsDirectVariety 𝓒 → (∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝓧 H → 𝓒 H) → 𝓒 G

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      (directVarietyClosure
        (fun (H : Type) [Group H] =>
          Finite (commutator H) ∨ (IsFCGroup H ∧ IsQuasicyclic (commutator H))) G ↔
        IsFCGroup G) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with finite derived
subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

That is, is the smallest class of groups closed under isomorphic copies, subgroups,
factor-groups and restricted direct products (over arbitrary index sets) that contains every
group $G$ with $G'$ finite and every $FC$-group $G$ with $G' \cong \mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for
some prime $p$ exactly the class of $FC$-groups?

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite (commutator G)] :
    IsFCGroup G := fun g => by
  refine ((commutator G : Set G).toFinite.image (g * ·)).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  refine ⟨⁅g⁻¹, c⁆,
    Subgroup.commutator_mem_commutator (Subgroup.mem_top _) (Subgroup.mem_top _), ?_⟩
  simp [commutatorElement_def, mul_assoc]

theorem isDirectVariety_directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) :
    IsDirectVariety (directVarietyClosure 𝓧) where
  of_mulEquiv e hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.of_mulEquiv e (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  subgroup H hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.subgroup H (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  quotient N _ hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.quotient N (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  restrictedProduct hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.restrictedProduct fun i => hG i 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H) (hG : IsFCGroup G) :
    IsFCGroup H := fun h => by
  refine ((hG (e.symm h)).image e).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  exact ⟨e.symm b, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨e.symm c, by simpa using congrArg e.symm hc⟩, by simp⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.quotient {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFCGroup G) (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] :
    IsFCGroup (G ⧸ N) := fun g => by
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective g
  refine ((hG g).image (QuotientGroup.mk (s := N))).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective c
  exact ⟨c * g * c⁻¹, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c, rfl⟩, by simpa using hc⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    (hG : ∀ i, IsFCGroup (G i)) : IsFCGroup (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))]) := fun x => by
  have hS : {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by simpa using x.2
  have hsub : ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ i, x i = 1 → y i = 1 := by
    intro y hy i hi
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    show c i * x i * (c i)⁻¹ = 1
    simp [hi]
  refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := fun y (i : hS.toFinset) => y i) ?_ ?_
  · refine (Set.Finite.pi' (t := fun (i : hS.toFinset) => conjugatesOf (x i))
      (fun i => hG _ _)).subset ?_
    rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c i, rfl⟩
  · intro y hy z hz h
    ext i
    by_cases hi : x i = 1
    · rw [hsub y hy i hi, hsub z hz i hi]
    · exact congrFun h ⟨i, hS.mem_toFinset.mpr hi⟩
blocks.docstring: A restricted direct product of $FC$-groups is an $FC$-group.
blocks.name: IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct

/-- A restricted direct product of $FC$-groups is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    (hG : ∀ i, IsFCGroup (G i)) : IsFCGroup (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))]) := fun x => by
  have hS : {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by simpa using x.2
  have hsub : ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ i, x i = 1 → y i = 1 := by
    intro y hy i hi
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    show c i * x i * (c i)⁻¹ = 1
    simp [hi]
  refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := fun y (i : hS.toFinset) => y i) ?_ ?_
  · refine (Set.Finite.pi' (t := fun (i : hS.toFinset) => conjugatesOf (x i))
      (fun i => hG _ _)).subset ?_
    rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c i, rfl⟩
  · intro y hy z hz h
    ext i
    by_cases hi : x i = 1
    · rw [hsub y hy i hi, hsub z hz i hi]
    · exact congrFun h ⟨i, hS.mem_toFinset.mpr hi⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: does the smallest class closed under subgroups, quotient groups and (restricted, arbitrary-index) direct products containing all groups with finite derived subgroup and all FC-groups with quasicyclic (Prüfer p-group, some prime p) derived subgroup equal the class of all FC-groups; 'direct product' must be the restricted direct product over arbitrary index sets (unrestricted Cartesian products of infinitely many nonabelian finite groups are not FC, contradicting the statement's 'FC-groups form a direct variety'), and since FC-groups already form a direct variety containing both generating classes the question is equivalent to every FC-group lying in the generated direct variety; the preceding sentences (Hall 1959, Kurdachenko 1987) are background facts, not questions.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful content (FC-groups = finite conjugacy classes; 'direct product' = restricted direct product over an arbitrary index type; quasicyclic = Prüfer p-group for a prime p; direct variety = isomorphism-closed class closed under subgroups, factor-groups and restricted products; generated variety = intersection of all such classes containing the generators; generating class = {G' finite} ∪ {FC with G' quasicyclic}). c01 was chosen because it uses the literal equality-of-classes form of the question (answer(True) ⇔ generated class = FC class), relies on Mathlib's RestrictedProduct (verified to be exactly finite-support families), and additionally proves, with real proofs, the notebook's remark that FC-groups form a direct variety under these definitions and that groups with finite derived subgroup are FC — this validates the 'restricted product' reading and shows the generated ⊆ FC inclusion holds, so the theorem is not trivially true/false for either answer. Only edit: parenthesized the inner ↔ in the main theorem to make the parse explicit (it was already parsed that way). Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning and passes `lake --wfail build` as a Kourovka module.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.16

by L. A. Kurdachenko

A class of groups is called a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking subgroups,
factor-groups, and direct products (Yu. M. Gorchakov, *Groups with Finite Classes of Conjugate
Elements*, Moscow, Nauka, 1978 (Russian)). It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a
direct variety. P. Hall (*J. London Math. Soc.*, **34**, no. 3 (1959), 289–304) showed that the
class of finite groups and the class of abelian groups taken together do not generate the class
of $FC$-groups as a direct variety, and it was shown in (L. A. Kurdachenko, *Ukrain. Math. J.*,
**39**, no. 3 (1987), 255–259) that the direct variety of $FC$-groups is also not generated by
the class of groups with finite derived subgroups. Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated
by the class of groups with finite derived subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups
having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

Here an $FC$-group is a group in which every element has only finitely many conjugates, and a
quasicyclic group is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$. "Direct product"
means the restricted direct product (only finitely many non-identity coordinates) over an
arbitrary index set: unrestricted Cartesian products of infinitely many non-abelian finite
groups are not $FC$-groups, so with unrestricted products the class of $FC$-groups would not be
a direct variety.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«10.16»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is an $FC$-group if every element of $G$ has only finitely many conjugates. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group is *quasicyclic* if it is a Prüfer group $\mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for some prime $p$,
i.e. isomorphic to the group of all complex $p^n$-th roots of unity, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. -/
def IsQuasicyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (p ^ n) ℂ))

/-- A class of groups (in the universe `u`), given as a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type (u + 1) :=
  ∀ (G : Type u) [Group G], Prop

/-- A class of groups is a *direct variety* if it is closed under taking isomorphic copies,
subgroups, factor-groups, and restricted direct products $\prod^{\text{res}}_{i \in I} G_i$
(all $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ with $x_i = 1$ for all but finitely many $i$) over arbitrary index
sets $I$. -/
structure IsDirectVariety (𝓒 : GroupClass.{u}) : Prop where
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  subgroup : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G), 𝓒 G → 𝓒 H
  quotient : ∀ {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝓒 G → 𝓒 (G ⧸ N)
  restrictedProduct : ∀ {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (G i)],
    (∀ i, 𝓒 (G i)) → 𝓒 (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))])

/-- The direct variety generated by a class of groups `𝓧`: the smallest direct variety
containing `𝓧`, i.e. the intersection of all direct varieties containing `𝓧`. -/
def directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) : GroupClass.{u} :=
  fun G _ => ∀ 𝓒 : GroupClass.{u},
    IsDirectVariety 𝓒 → (∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝓧 H → 𝓒 H) → 𝓒 G

/--
Is the direct variety of $FC$-groups generated by the class of groups with finite derived
subgroups together with the class of $FC$-groups having quasicyclic derived subgroups?

That is, is the smallest class of groups closed under isomorphic copies, subgroups,
factor-groups and restricted direct products (over arbitrary index sets) that contains every
group $G$ with $G'$ finite and every $FC$-group $G$ with $G' \cong \mathbb{Z}(p^\infty)$ for
some prime $p$ exactly the class of $FC$-groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      (directVarietyClosure
        (fun (H : Type) [Group H] =>
          Finite (commutator H) ∨ (IsFCGroup H ∧ IsQuasicyclic (commutator H))) G ↔
        IsFCGroup G) := by
  sorry

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFCGroup_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

/-- Every abelian group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFCGroup_of_isMulCommutative (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsMulCommutative G] :
    IsFCGroup G :=
  fun g => (Set.finite_singleton g).subset fun _ hb => by simpa [eq_comm] using isConj_iff_eq.mp hb

/-- Every group with finite derived subgroup is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite (commutator G)] :
    IsFCGroup G := fun g => by
  refine ((commutator G : Set G).toFinite.image (g * ·)).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  refine ⟨⁅g⁻¹, c⁆,
    Subgroup.commutator_mem_commutator (Subgroup.mem_top _) (Subgroup.mem_top _), ?_⟩
  simp [commutatorElement_def, mul_assoc]

/-- The group of all complex $2^n$-th roots of unity is quasicyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isQuasicyclic_rootsOfUnity_two : IsQuasicyclic ↥(⨆ n : ℕ, rootsOfUnity (2 ^ n) ℂ) :=
  ⟨2, Nat.prime_two, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The direct variety generated by `𝓧` contains `𝓧`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_directVarietyClosure {𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}} {G : Type u} [Group G] (hG : 𝓧 G) :
    directVarietyClosure 𝓧 G :=
  fun _ _ h𝓧 => h𝓧 G hG

/-- The direct variety generated by `𝓧` is a direct variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isDirectVariety_directVarietyClosure (𝓧 : GroupClass.{u}) :
    IsDirectVariety (directVarietyClosure 𝓧) where
  of_mulEquiv e hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.of_mulEquiv e (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  subgroup H hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.subgroup H (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  quotient N _ hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.quotient N (hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧)
  restrictedProduct hG 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧 := h𝓒.restrictedProduct fun i => hG i 𝓒 h𝓒 h𝓧

/-- An isomorphic copy of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H) (hG : IsFCGroup G) :
    IsFCGroup H := fun h => by
  refine ((hG (e.symm h)).image e).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  exact ⟨e.symm b, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨e.symm c, by simpa using congrArg e.symm hc⟩, by simp⟩

/-- A subgroup of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFCGroup G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    IsFCGroup H := fun h => by
  refine ((hG h).preimage Subtype.val_injective.injOn).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c, by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hc⟩

/-- A factor-group of an $FC$-group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.quotient {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFCGroup G) (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] :
    IsFCGroup (G ⧸ N) := fun g => by
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective g
  refine ((hG g).image (QuotientGroup.mk (s := N))).subset fun b hb => ?_
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hb
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective c
  exact ⟨c * g * c⁻¹, isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c, rfl⟩, by simpa using hc⟩

/-- A restricted direct product of $FC$-groups is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    (hG : ∀ i, IsFCGroup (G i)) : IsFCGroup (Πʳ i, [G i, (⊥ : Subgroup (G i))]) := fun x => by
  have hS : {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by simpa using x.2
  have hsub : ∀ y ∈ conjugatesOf x, ∀ i, x i = 1 → y i = 1 := by
    intro y hy i hi
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    show c i * x i * (c i)⁻¹ = 1
    simp [hi]
  refine Set.Finite.of_finite_image (f := fun y (i : hS.toFinset) => y i) ?_ ?_
  · refine (Set.Finite.pi' (t := fun (i : hS.toFinset) => conjugatesOf (x i))
      (fun i => hG _ _)).subset ?_
    rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := isConj_iff.mp hy
    exact isConj_iff.mpr ⟨c i, rfl⟩
  · intro y hy z hz h
    ext i
    by_cases hi : x i = 1
    · rw [hsub y hy i hi, hsub z hz i hi]
    · exact congrFun h ⟨i, hS.mem_toFinset.mpr hi⟩

/-- "It is obvious that the class of $FC$-groups is a direct variety." -/
@[category textbook, AMS 20]
theorem isDirectVariety_isFCGroup :
    IsDirectVariety (fun (G : Type u) [Group G] => IsFCGroup G) where
  of_mulEquiv e hG := hG.of_mulEquiv e
  subgroup H hG := hG.subgroup H
  quotient N _ hG := hG.quotient N
  restrictedProduct hG := IsFCGroup.restrictedProduct hG

end Kourovka.«10.16»

items: 'Direct product' is taken to be the restricted direct product (finitely many non-identity coordinates) over an arbitrary index set, per the decomposition notes; with this reading the file proves (textbook theorem `isDirectVariety_isFCGroup`) the notebook's remark that FC-groups form a direct variety, which would be false for unrestricted products.
Closure under isomorphic copies is included in `IsDirectVariety` (a 'class of groups' is by convention isomorphism-closed); without it the type-theoretic 'smallest class' would be artificially small.

The question is stated as an equality of classes (`directVarietyClosure 𝓧 G ↔ IsFCGroup G` for all G), i.e. literally 'the generated direct variety is the class of FC-groups'; the inclusion generated ⊆ FC is a true fact (FC is a direct variety containing the generators, see `IsFCGroup.of_finite_commutator` and `isDirectVariety_isFCGroup`), so this agrees with the notes' reading 'every FC-group lies in the generated class'.
Quasicyclic = Prüfer p-group ℤ(p^∞) for some prime p, modelled concretely as the group of all complex p^n-th roots of unity, up to isomorphism (`Nonempty (G ≃* ...)`).
'Derived subgroup' is Mathlib's `commutator H = ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆`, coerced to a type for `Finite`/`IsQuasicyclic`.
Groups, index sets and classes live in universe `Type` (universe 0) in the main statement, following the repository's Kourovka files; the definitions themselves are universe-polymorphic.

Extra proved API/test lemmas (FC-groups closed under iso, subgroups, quotients, restricted products; finite/abelian/finite-derived groups are FC; the 2-power roots of unity are quasicyclic; the closure is a direct variety containing 𝓧) are included as sanity checks of the bespoke definitions. The Hall (1959) and Kurdachenko (1987) background facts are quoted in the module docstring but not formalized, as the decomposition table marks them background.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities resolved (and documented in the module docstring): (1) 'direct product' is the restricted direct product (finitely many non-identity coordinates) over arbitrary index sets — the only reading consistent with the statement's 'FC-groups form a direct variety' (unrestricted Cartesian products of infinitely many nonabelian finite groups are not FC) and with Hall/Kurdachenko's cited results being non-trivial (finite products only would make the class of groups with finite derived subgroup already closed); this matches Gorchakov's/Russian usage. (2) Classes of groups are taken isomorphism-closed (standard convention; needed since Lean subgroups/quotients/products are specific types). (3) All groups and index sets live in `Type`, following the other Kourovka files; every group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, so nothing is lost. The equality form was preferred to the equivalent inclusion form (c04/c05/c08) as the more literal rendering; the two are provably equivalent given the proven textbook theorem in the file. No candidate was unfaithful; differences were in presentation (rootsOfUnity vs primaryComponent vs intrinsic chain characterization of ℤ(p^∞); hand-rolled vs Mathlib restricted product; c07's injective/surjective-hom closure). c02's API lemmas lacked AMS tags (style only). The Hall (1959) and Kurdachenko (1987) sentences are background facts and were not formalized, per the decomposition table.
